==English==

===Alternative forms===
* {{alter|en|receave|receyve||obsolete}}

===Etymology===
{{root|en|ine-pro|*keh₂p-}}
From {{inh|en|enm|receyven}}, from {{der|en|fro|recevoir|receivre}}, from {{der|en|la|recipiō|recipere|t=take back, accept, etc.}}, from {{m|la|re-||back}} + {{m|la|capiō||to take}}; see [[capacious]]. Compare [[conceive]], [[deceive]], [[perceive]]. Displaced native {{cog|enm|-}} terms in {{m|enm|fon|-fon}}/{{m|enm|fangen|-fangen}} (e.g. {{m|enm|afon}}, {{m|enm|anfon}}, {{m|enm|afangen}}, {{m|enm|underfangen}}, etc. "to receive" from {{cog|ang|fon|-fōn}}), native {{cog|enm|thiggen||to receive}} (from {{cog|ang|þiċġan}}), and non-native {{cog|enm|aquilen}}, {{m|enm|enquilen||to receive}} (from {{cog|fro|aquillir}}, {{m|fro|encueillir}}).

===Pronunciation===
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈsiːv/|a=RP}}
* {{IPA|en|/ɹɪˈsiv/|a=GA,CA}}
* {{audio|en|en-us-receive.ogg|a=US}}
* {{hyphenation|en|re|ceive}}
* {{rhymes|en|iːv|s=2}}

===Verb===
{{en-verb}}

# {{lb|en|transitive}} To be [[give]]n, [[send|sent]], or [[pay|paid]] something.
#: {{ux|en|He '''received''' many presents for his birthday.}}
#* {{RQ:Maxwell Mirror and the Lamp|chapter=XXXIX|page=305|passage=Nothing was too small to '''receive''' attention, if a supervising eye could suggest improvements likely to conduce to the common welfare. Mr. Gordon Burnage, for instance, personally visited dust-bins and back premises, accompanied by a sort of village bailiff, going his round like a commanding officer doing billets.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive|dated}} To [[take]], as something that is [[offer]]ed; to [[accept]].
#: {{ux|en|He had the offer of employment, but he would not '''receive''' it.}}
#* {{RQ:Shakespeare All's Well|act=II|scene=i|page=235|column=1|passage=Our hearts '''receiue''' your warnings.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|1 Kings|8|64|url=https://archive.org/stream/Bible1611/Binder1#page/n451/mode/1up|column=1|passage=[T]he braſen Altar that was before the {{smallcaps|Lord}} was too little to '''receiue''' the burnt offerings, and meat offerings, and the fat of the peace offerings.}}
#* {{quote-book|en|author=Thomas Wimberley Mossman|quotee={{w|Pope Clement I}} (in translation)|chapter=The Genuine and Supposititious Writings of St. Clement|title=A History of the Catholic Church of Jesus Christ: From the Death of [[w:John the Evangelist|Saint John]] to the Middle of the Second Century:{{nb...|Including an Account of the Original Organisation of the Christian Ministry and the Growth of Episcopacy.}}|location=London|publisher=[[w:Longman|Longmans, Green, and Co.]]|year=1873|page=58|pageurl=https://books.google.com/books?id=xZMvAAAAYAAJ&pg=PA58|oclc=59217512|passage=And afterwards Thou [God] '''receivedst''' {{w|Seth}} and [[w:Enoch (ancestor of Noah)|Enoch]], and Enoch Thou translatedst; for Thou art the Creator of men, the Fountain of Life, the Supplier of Want, the Giver of Laws, the Rewarder of them that keep them, the Avenger of them that transgress them.}}
# {{lb|en|law}} To [[take]] [[goods]] knowing them to be [[steal|stolen]].
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[act]] as a [[host]] for [[guest]]s; to give [[admittance]] to; to [[permit]] to [[enter]], as into one's [[house]], [[presence]], [[company]], etc.
#: {{syn|en|have|}}
#: {{ux|en|to '''receive''' a lodger, visitor, ambassador, messenger, etc.}}
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Acts|28|2|url=https://archive.org/stream/Bible1611/Binder1#page/n1383/mode/1up|column=1|passage=And the barbarous people ſhewed vs no little kindneſſe: for they kindled a fire, and '''receiued''' us euery one becauſe of the preſent raine, and becauſe of the cold.}}
#* {{RQ:Besant Ivory Gate|chapter=The Select Circle|page=46|passage=In former days every tavern of repute kept such a room for the select circle—a club, or society, of ''habitués'', who met every evening for a pipe and a cheerful glass. [...] Strangers might enter the room, but they were made to feel that they were there on sufferance; they were '''received''' with distance and suspicion.}}
# {{lb|en|transitive}} To [[incur]] (an [[injury]]).
#: {{ux|en|I '''received''' a bloody nose from the collision.}}
# To [[allow]] (a [[custom]], [[tradition]], etc.); to give [[credence]] or [[acceptance]] to.
#* {{RQ:King James Version|Mark|7|3|4|url=https://archive.org/stream/Bible1611/Binder1#page/n1264/mode/1up|column=2|passage=For the Phariſes and all the Jewes, except they waſh their hands oft, eate not, holding the tradition of the elders. And when they come from the market, except they waſh, they eate not. And many other things there be, which they have '''receiued''' to hold, as the waſhing of cups and pots, braſen veſſels, and of tables.}}
# {{lb|en|telecommunications}} To [[detect]] a [[signal]] from a [[transmitter]].
# {{lb|en|sports}} To be in a [[position]] to take [[possession]], or [[hit]] [[back]] the [[ball]].
## {{lb|en|tennis|badminton|squash}} To be in a position to hit back a [[service]].
## {{lb|en|American football}} To be in a position to [[catch]] a [[forward pass]].
# {{lb|en|transitive|intransitive}} To accept into the [[mind]]; to [[understand]].
#* {{RQ:Montaigne Florio Essayes|chapter=57|book=I|passage=I cannot '''receive''' {{transterm|frm|recevoir}} that manner, whereby we establish the continuance of our life.}}
